csv_project_name: DB for Lewis House Relocation Restoration & Reconstruction
csv_scope_of_work: The City of Longwood, Florida ( City ) hereby requests Statements of Qualifications from qualified firms to provide design-build services for the relocation, restoration, and reconstruction of the historic Lewis House (circa 1885), located within Downtown Longwood Florida. The purpose of this project is to preserve and restore the historic Lewis House and relocate it to Reiter Park for use as a small public assembly space for meetings and community gatherings. The structure, originally constructed circa 1885, has been relocated multiple times and has been stored on a City-owned parcel for approximately ten years following donation to the City. The selected Respondent shall provide complete design-build services and shall be solely responsible for the completeness, coordination, and code compliance of all design and construction services required to deliver the Project. The Project shall be delivered using a design-build approach, and the selected Contractor shall provide all architectural, engineering, permitting, relocation, restoration, reconstruction, construction, supervision, and coordination services necessary to complete the Project. Deliverables The Contractor shall provide, at a minimum, the following: Identification of original materials that can be safely salvaged and reused, together with a written plan describing the most cost-effective method for relocating and incorporating salvageable elements into the reconstructed structure. Preparation of complete, code-compliant architectural and engineering plans suitable for permitting through the City of Longwood Building Division, including reconstruction of the original front porch. Coordination and submission of permit applications. Permit fees shall be paid by the City. Safe relocation of the structure and construction of a historically appropriate foundation system. Full construction, painting, finishing, and completion of the building and all associated site elements, including a brick entrance walkway and required utility connections. Interior Specifications The restored structure shall be adapted for small public assembly use and shall comply with applicable provisions of the Florida Building Code. The first floor shall be designed as an open floor space suitable for small gatherings, meetings, and rental events. A second floor shall be constructed in a manner similar to its existing condition and may be utilized for storage purposes. Interior walls shall consist of beadboard finished with white paint and include modern insulation as required by code. Flooring shall be durable and suitable for anticipated foot traffic and functional transitions. A suitable air conditioning system shall be installed and designed to minimize visual impact to the exterior of the building. The base response shall include one (1) ADA-compliant unisex restroom integrated into the design in accordance with the Florida Building Code and Florida Accessibility Code. For purposes of uniform pricing and design assumptions, the interior occupant load shall be assumed to be ten (10) persons, exclusive of the porch area, and the building shall be designed for Assembly Group A-3 occupancy. Exterior Specifications The exterior restoration shall preserve the historic character of the structure and incorporate documented architectural elements. Reconstruction shall include the addition of the original full-length front porch. The porch shall span the length of the structure and be of sufficient width to accommodate rocking chairs or a rocking bench. The historic rear bump-out section shall be incorporated into the design and may be utilized to accommodate the required restroom. Side doors shall not be carried over into the reconstructed building. Doors shall be located at the front and rear only. Side elevations shall include large windows consistent in style with the original structure. The building shall be supported on red-brick piers or other historically appropriate foundation elements that promote air circulation and mitigate moisture intrusion. Roofing shall consist of 24-gauge standing seam metal in a crow s foot profile. Final color selection shall match existing pavilion roofs within Reiter Park and shall be subject to City approval. Gutters shall be incorporated in a manner consistent with the historic design. ADA access shall be thoughtfully integrated into site planning and building design to minimize aesthetic impact. Front and rear doors shall be restored or replicated consistent with original specifications. Exterior siding shall consist of horizontal wood clapboard using cypress or cedar (not pine). Windows shall be restored or replicated consistent with original specifications. Where feasible, antique glass may be preserved or incorporated; otherwise, modern insulated glazing may be used for energy efficiency Exterior paint colors shall retain the building s historic light blue body with darker blue accents. Final color selections shall be subject to City approval. Historically appropriate materials and suppliers, such as Florida Victorian Architectural Salvage or similar sources, may be utilized where feasible. Building Access Walkway Specifications The Contractor shall provide a pedestrian access walkway constructed of red brick pavers consistent in appearance and quality with existing park walkways. Brick pavers shall be durable, uniform in color and size, and suitable for future engraving if the City elects to implement such a program. The walkway shall comply with all applicable ADA accessibility requirements, including slope, cross-slope, width, and surface stability. Product specifications, samples, and color selections shall be submitted to the City for review and approval prior to installation. Installation shall follow manufacturer recommendations and industry standards to ensure longterm performance.
